title: sagina procumbens subsp. corsica
intro: Sagina procumbens subsp. corsica, commonly known as Corsican pearlwort, is a subspecies of flowering plant in the family Caryophyllaceae. It is a perennial plant that has been traditionally used for its medicinal properties, with reported health benefits including anti-inflammatory and antioxidant effects. The therapeutic actions of Sagina procumbens subsp. corsica are attributed to its bioactive constituents, which include phenolic compounds, flavonoids, and terpenoids, that are believed to exert anti-inflammatory, antimicrobial, and antioxidant actions. However, more research is needed to fully understand the health benefits and therapeutic actions of this plant.
